Date: 2026-12-08

Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Jared (Acme Head of ML), Priya (Acme Security), Tom (Acme Platform), Mei (Acme Product)

Summary: Align on POC goals and benchmarks; prefer quick hosted start for proofs, evaluate Dedicated for cost predictability and Private for data residency/security.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we wanted to spend the hour on scoping the POC and make sure we capture the success metrics and how to compare hosted vs dedicated vs private, sound good?
[00:08] Jared: Yeah, that sounds great. Quick note, we kinda have two use cases, one is near-real-time credit decisioning where latency matters, and the other is batch enrichment overnight.
[00:16] Liam: ok that's helpful, so we should size both tails - the low-latency 99th percentile and the batch throughput. Do you have current qps numbers?
[00:23] Tom: Right now our decisioning service does around 60 qps peak, but spiky, like up to 120 for short bursts. Batch is roughly 5M records nightly.
[00:33] Priya: From security side we need SOC 2 and ISO 27001 compliance, audit logs, and customer data must remain in our EU region for PII. We also have a requirement to rotate keys via our KMS, and we prefer bring-your-own-key for the private option.
[00:46] Liam: got it, for hosted we support region pinning and customer-managed KMS integrations on enterprise plans, for private we obviously can do full VPC/on-prem with HSM. There might be slight latency tradeoffs on private depending on network topology.
[01:00] Mei: timeline, we are targeting a Q1 production decision, so the POC needs to finish by mid-January. Is that doable?
[01:06] Samira: Yes, we can do a two-phase POC: Phase one hosted pilot for functional validation and latency baselining - 2 weeks. Phase two, parallel dedicated sizing and private feasibility - 3 weeks. Total ~5 weeks including benchmark runs and analysis.
[01:20] Jared: ok what's the success criteria? For us it's primarily 99th percentile latency under 200ms for decisioning, accuracy parity within 2% relative to our baseline model, and cost per 1,000 decisions under a target - we haven't nailed the dollar figure yet but we'll share targets.
[01:33] Liam: that's concrete, we'll run a targeted benchmark: 1) single-request latency profile for 60 qps with 2x burst, 2) tail-latency 99p, 3) batch throughput for the nightly job, and 4) output quality check against your testset. We'll provide scripts and a sample harness.
[01:49] Priya: About data residency - if we do hosted, what guarantees do you provide?
[01:52] Samira: For hosted we can pin to EU region on the enterprise tier and maintain logs retention in region. For additional compliance we can route through our enterprise controls and provide SOC2 reports. The private option is the only way to have Acme-managed network/HSM.
[02:06] Tom: For dedicated, is the hardware reserved? We're trying to understand pricing predictability for steady-state.
[02:10] Liam: Dedicated is reserved capacity with predictable throughput. You get a GPU pool sized for your expected qps, with autoscaling policies and burst allowances. Pricing is monthly commit based - good if you have steady throughput. Hosted favors variable usage but can be more costly at scale unless you use caching/batching optimizations.
[02:26] Jared: We also care about model rollout and versioning - our product team wants canary deploys and quick rollback. How do those work across modes?
[02:32] Samira: Same API abstraction across all modes. The console supports canary policies, A/B rollout, and automatic fallback to a lighter model if the primary fails. That works in hosted and dedicated; private can include the same control plane or a customer-managed control plane depending on contract.
[02:48] Mei: For benchmarks, what dataset should we use? We can give a representative sample of 50k decisioning queries and the nightly batch subset.
[02:54] Liam: 50k is perfect for initial latencies and QC. For batch, provide a 100k sample slice that mirrors cardinality and token lengths. We'll run the harness and give a report with token-level cost estimates.
[03:06] Priya: One concern - full transcripts of PII in logs. How are logs handled?
[03:09] Samira: We can redact PII at the SDK layer and ensure request/response logs are optionally disabled; for enterprise we support encrypted audit logs and retention policies. We'll include the security pack in the deck.
[03:19] Jared: On the decision criteria matrix - can we summarize tradeoffs?
[03:22] Liam: Sure - Hosted: fastest to get started, good for iteration, region pinning available, less predictable costs at scale, easier for short POCs. Dedicated: best for predictable throughput and cost efficiency at scale, reserved hardware, suits steady real-time workloads. Private: necessary for strict data residency and audit controls, more setup/time and potentially higher latency depending on deployment.
[03:41] Tom: Are there known performance deltas between dedicated and hosted? Like do you see lower latency on dedicated due to reserved GPUs and kernel optimizations?
[03:47] Liam: Dedicated can give more consistent tail latency because of dedicated GPU pools and optimized kernel selection for your workload. Hosted is multi-tenant but we've got performance profiles; if you need ultra-consistent 99p, dedicated often is the better bet.
[03:58] Mei: For the POC schedule can we lock dates now?
[04:01] Samira: Proposed: 1) 2026-12-13: send POC plan and scripts; 2) 2026-12-15 to 2026-12-29: hosted pilot and initial latency baselining (two weeks including analysis); 3) 2026-12-20 to 2027-01-05: dedicated sizing runs and private feasibility (overlapping); 4) 2027-01-10: Decision meeting with results. Does that align?
[04:19] Jared: Works for us but we'll confirm resource availability. Priya - security review needed before any private infra access?
[04:24] Priya: Yes, we'll need an NDA addendum and a short architecture review; timeline dependent but we can expedite for the POC.
[04:30] Samira: We'll include the security questionnaire and SOC2 report in the send. Also I'll add the KMS BYOK steps for private.
[04:36] Jared: On acceptance criteria - if hosted pilot meets latency and accuracy but costs look high at scale, are we comfortable moving to dedicated? Basically hosted for quick proof, dedicated to optimize cost if numbers work out?
[04:46] Liam: That's the typical path. We'll show modeled cost per 1k decisions based on your qps distribution and batching. If dedicated reduces unit cost and meets latency SLOs, we recommend dedicated. If data residency blocks hosted/dedicated, private is the fallback.
[04:59] Mei: Any blockers we should prepare for?
[05:02] Samira: Provide traffic profile, test dataset slices, any shaped prompts, and SLOs. Also security point of contact for the questionnaire.
[05:10] Tom: We'll prepare the traffic export and a small sandbox account.
[05:13] Samira: Great. Quick recap of next steps?
[05:15] Jared: Samira to send POC plan and pricing by Friday (2026-12-10). Liam shares benchmark harness. Acme sends datasets and traffic profile by Monday (2026-12-13). Schedule load test week of 2026-12-20.
[05:30] Samira: Perfect thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with the deck and security pack.
[05:35] Jared: Thanks, bye.
